verses.text: When the seventh month had come, and the children of Israel were in the cities, the people gathered themselves together as one man to Jerusalem.

Then Jeshua the son of Jozadak stood up with his brothers the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and his brothers, and built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the law of Moses the man of God.
In spite of their fear because of the peoples of the surrounding lands, they set the altar on its base; and they offered burnt offerings on it to Yahweh, even burnt offerings morning and evening.
They kept the feast of tents, as it is written, and offered the daily burnt offerings by number, according to the ordinance, as the duty of every day required;
and afterward the continual burnt offering, the offerings of the new moons, of all the set feasts of Yahweh that were consecrated, and of everyone who willingly offered a freewill offering to Yahweh.
From the first day of the seventh month, they began to offer burnt offerings to Yahweh; but the foundation of Yahweh’s temple was not yet laid.

They also gave money to the masons, and to the carpenters. They also gave food, drink, and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre, to bring cedar trees from Lebanon to the sea, to Joppa, according to the grant that they had from Cyrus King of Persia.

Now in the second year of their coming to God’s house at Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and the rest of their brothers the priests and the Levites, and all those who had come out of the captivity to Jerusalem, began the work and appointed the Levites, from twenty years old and upward, to have the oversight of the work of Yahweh’s house.

Then Jeshua stood with his sons and his brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, together, to have the oversight of the workmen in God’s house: the sons of Henadad, with their sons and their brothers the Levites.

When the builders laid the foundation of Yahweh’s temple, they set the priests in their clothing with trumpets, with the Levites the sons of Asaph with cymbals, to praise Yahweh, according to the directions of David king of Israel.

They sang to one another in praising and giving thanks to Yahweh, “For he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever toward Israel.” All the people shouted with a great shout, when they praised Yahweh, because the foundation of Yahweh’s house had been laid.

But many of the priests and Levites and heads of fathers’ households, the old men who had seen the first house, when the foundation of this house was laid before their eyes, wept with a loud voice. Many also shouted aloud for joy,
so that the people could not discern the noise of the shout of joy from the noise of the weeping of the people; for the people shouted with a loud shout, and the noise was heard far away.

footnotes.content: After seventy years in exile, the people gather as one—no divisions, no hesitation. There's a tender weight in how brokenness draws us back to the place where God promised to dwell. When we come home to Him, we come together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeshua and Zerubbabel act as one—priests and builders, brothers standing side by side. Notice they don't hesitate or consult: they rebuild the altar 'as it is written in the law of Moses.' That steady obedience to what God spoke long ago is their anchor.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fear surrounds them—enemies all around—yet they set the altar on its base and worship anyway. This is the quiet courage of the returning remnant: you offer burnt offerings not when danger is gone, but *in spite of* it. That's where faith shows its true grain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They keep the feast of tents and the daily offerings by the book—law-keeping that echoes worship. Every ritual, every morning and evening sacrifice, declares: *We remember who we are. We belong to the God who brought us home.* Obedience becomes remembrance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The new moons, the set feasts, the freewill offerings—all rise from one flame. Notice the 'willingly offered' part: some bring extra, moved by gratitude that won't be kept. The Lord stirs generous hearts among His returning people, and the altar receives both obedience and love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A haunting detail: they worship faithfully, but the temple foundation isn't yet laid. They offer to the Lord with empty hands in one sense—no great house, no finished work. Yet praise rises anyway. Sometimes the most honest worship happens when we have nothing to show but our obedience and our hope.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They give to masons and carpenters, feed the workers from Sidon and Tyre—and those strangers supply cedar from Lebanon. Grace works in practical ways: money, tools, labor, provision. The Lord's house rises because His people invest themselves and their resources with open hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In the second year, the work begins in earnest. Zerubbabel and Jeshua appoint Levites from twenty years old and up—a whole generation born or grown in exile, who've never seen the first temple. The Lord trusts the future of His house to those who must rebuild what they've never known.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeshua, Kadmiel, Henadad—names woven through the work. These aren't distant builders; they're brothers, fathers, sons, all laboring together. The Lord's house is built not by a lone genius, but by families and clans who agree to carry one burden together. That's how His kingdom grows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When the foundation stone is laid, the priests dress in their sacred clothing, trumpets sound, cymbals crash—David's ancient music joins the ancient rite. The Lord is praised, not in quiet, but in the full voice of His people. Joy and worship overflow the ordinary work of laying stone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'For He is good, for His loving kindness endures forever toward Israel.' That psalm, sung by the remnant standing on the foundation of their God's house—what a moment. They've sung it in exile in their hearts. Now they sing it on the very ground where He promised to dwell again with them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The old men who saw the first temple weep aloud; others shout in joy. Grief and gladness break from the same deep place. These elders grieve what was lost—that glorious house of Solomon—yet rejoice that the Lord hasn't abandoned His people. Both tears and shouts honor Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo: weeping and shouting blend into one great noise that travels far. The world hears something from God's people that they cannot quite sort—is it loss or victory? Often it's both, held together by a faith that the Lord who grieves with us also gives us reason to rejoice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
